hotspots.name: Notice Board
hotspots.examine: A notice board covered in printouts. One catches your eye — a password reminder from 'IT Support'.

hotspots.name: Reception Desk
hotspots.examine: The reception desk. A sign reads: 'All visitors must sign in. Tailgating is a security violation.'

hotspots.name: Security Poster
hotspots.examine: A Government of Canada security awareness poster. It says: 'Think Before You Click. Report Suspicious Emails.'

hotspots.name: Suspicious Briefcase
hotspots.examine: A briefcase with a USB drive sticking out of the pocket. It looks like it was left here deliberately.

hotspots.name: Unknown USB Drive
hotspots.examine: A USB drive sitting on top of a server. Someone may have left it here, or planted it.

hotspots.name: Server Rack
hotspots.examine: A rack of servers humming quietly. The blinking lights make it look alive. No external devices should be connected to these.

hotspots.name: Access Log Terminal
hotspots.examine: A terminal showing the access log. You notice Wanda's badge was scanned in twice this morning — but she didn't sign the visitor log.

lines.speaker: justin
lines.text: There's a notice pinned up here: 'Urgent — Please reset your password by clicking the link below. — IT Support.' Something feels off.

lines.speaker: smarty
lines.text: Psst — Justin. Before you do anything, what do you usually check in an email like that?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You click the link. A fake login page appears. Your credentials are now compromised. Wanda smiles from across the lobby.

lines.speaker: smarty
lines.text: Hmm. What could you have checked before clicking that link?

choices.label: Check the sender's email address first

lines.speaker: justin
lines.text: I look at the sender: 'it-support@gov-ca-helpdesk.net'. That's not a government domain. That's a red flag.

choices.label: Report it to IT Security without clicking

lines.speaker: justin
lines.text: I forward the notice details to itsecurity@canada.ca and mark it as suspected phishing.

lines.speaker: smarty
lines.text: That's exactly right. Reporting suspicious communications protects everyone on the network. Well done!

lines.speaker: smarty
lines.text: Good catch. Now that you know it's suspicious — what's the right next step?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Others might still fall for it. Deleting without reporting leaves the threat active.

lines.speaker: justin
lines.text: I report the suspicious notice to IT Security immediately.

lines.speaker: smarty
lines.text: Perfect. You stopped potential harm to the whole network.

lines.speaker: smarty
lines.text: What can you do right now to limit the damage from clicking that link?

choices.label: Report it to IT Security and change my password

lines.speaker: justin
lines.text: I call IT Security right away and change my password from a secure device.

lines.speaker: smarty
lines.text: Fast action after an incident matters. You may have limited the exposure.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The incident goes unreported. The attacker maintains access for days.

lines.speaker: justin
lines.text: An unknown USB drive just sitting here on the server. It could be anything.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: USB drives found in unexpected places are a classic social engineering attack. They may contain malware that auto-runs when inserted.

choices.label: Plug it in to see what's on it

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The moment it's connected, a script runs. The server room lights flicker. Something is spreading across the network.

lines.speaker: smarty
lines.text: What should you have done instead of plugging it in?

choices.label: Leave it alone and report it to Security

lines.speaker: justin
lines.text: I don't touch it. I photograph it with my phone and call IT Security to report a suspicious device.

lines.speaker: smarty
lines.text: Exactly right. Never plug in unknown devices. Report and let trained staff handle it.

choices.label: Pocket it to examine later on a personal device

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your personal device is compromised within seconds of plugging it in.

lines.speaker: smarty
lines.text: Unknown devices are dangerous on any machine — personal or government. What's the safe move?

lines.speaker: justin
lines.text: The access log shows Wanda's badge scanned twice today — but I saw her in the lobby, not in here. And she didn't sign the physical log.

choices.label: Ignore it — probably a system glitch

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Possible tailgating incidents left uninvestigated are a real insider threat risk.

choices.label: Report the anomaly to the Security Officer

lines.speaker: justin
lines.text: I flag the access log anomaly to the building Security Officer.

lines.speaker: smarty
lines.text: Good. Unusual access patterns are worth reporting. It could be nothing — or it could be tailgating. Either way, it's not your call to ignore it.

lines.speaker: justin
lines.text: The briefcase has a USB drive in the pocket. It wasn't there an hour ago.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A USB drive left unattended in a public area of a government building. Wanda is nowhere to be seen.

choices.label: Take the USB drive to examine it

lines.speaker: smarty
lines.text: Hmm. What are the risks of handling unknown devices taken from a stranger's belongings?

choices.label: Report the unattended bag and USB to Security

lines.speaker: justin
lines.text: I alert building security about an unattended bag with an exposed USB drive.

lines.speaker: smarty
lines.text: Correct. Unattended items in secure areas are a physical security concern — not just a techincal one.

reporter.name: First Responder
reporter.desc: Reported a suspicious communication or device to IT Security.

usb_aware.name: USB Aware
usb_aware.desc: Refused to plug in an unknown USB device and reported it.

vigilant.name: Vigilant
vigilant.desc: Noticed and reported an access log anomaly.

quick_recovery.name: Quick Recovery
quick_recovery.desc: Reported a phishing incident and changed credentials promptly after clicking a bad link.

data_guardian.name: Data Guardian
data_guardian.desc: Completed both modules without triggering a high-risk outcome.
